text:
dmitri: quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector rollout last night I'm seeing a p99 host-parse bump on prod :eyes:
ops-bot: alert: canary p99_host_parse +28% (service=runtime-ingress, region=us-west-2, window=5m)
dmitri: baseline was ~12ms, now p99 ~24ms for short chat requests (<=32 tokens)
ben: any signs it's KV cache or batching?
dmitri: looked at top-of-stack traces, host-side tokenize + parse moved from ~20% -> ~45% of request CPU
elaine: interesting — we also changed kernel preference for small-seq models to favor fp16 kernels. could be a mismatch causing extra copy/transpose on host
carol: also saw an increase in small-write frames over gRPC after the change — more tiny packets, more framing overhead
dmitri: adding a small profiler dump from a repro run on canary VMs:
```
PROFILE SAMPLE (short request)
host_parse_tokenize: 11.8ms
host_proto_unmarshal: 2.6ms
host_frame_writev: 3.9ms
host_kv_cache_lookup: 0.7ms
serving_kernel_dispatch: 6.3ms
other: 0.9ms
TOTAL: 26.2ms
```
ben: writev at 3.9ms is suspicious for tiny-write storm. are we flush-on-every-chunk now?
dmitri: looks like streaming-chunker now emits smaller chunks for preparse path, and the scheduler hints reduced coalescing to keep latency low — but cost is many syscalls
elaine: kernel-selector might have changed the expected seq-length distribution, so preparse split heuristic decided to favor immediate dispatch rather than pack with following frames
carol: can we instrument the chunker to report chunk-size histogram and whether coalesce was attempted? add a counter for coalesce_fired yes/no
dmitri: on it. also going to toggle the kernel hint to prefer the legacy small-seq path on canary and remeasure
ops-bot: deploy-started: dmitri/host-preparse-probe -> canary (3 hosts)
ben: while we're at it, add KV cache hit/miss timing per-request in the trace so we can rule out eviction thrashing
dmitri: good call. current traces show kvcache lookup cheap but we don't have hot-shard metrics per-req
elaine: quick experiment idea: revert the kernel-selector step that flipped small-seq preference, keep batching heuristic change. if latency drops, selector is culprit
carol: another low-effort mitigation: increase write coalesce window from 1ms -> 3ms for streaming responses for <=64 byte chunks. might lose a bit of tail latency but reduce CPU/syscall load
dmitri: schedule: i'll push the kernel revert to canary in 10m and enable chunker histogram logs. will report back in 20m.
ben: ack. if that doesn't show improvement, we should capture tcpdump on one canary host to measure packetization
elaine: also check the serving runtime's kernel-to-hardware mapping logs — if dispatch is doing an extra memcpy to align to kernel primitives that explains host copy time
dmitri: todo list summarized: 1) instrument chunker hist + coalesce counter 2) enable per-req KV shard timings 3) revert kernel-selector small-seq preference on canary 4) optional: bump write coalesce window on canary 5) capture tcpdump if needed
carol: add me to the follow-up. i can help with tcpdump + parsing
ops-bot: deploy-finished: canary updated (3 hosts) -> monitor 10m
dmitri: initial numbers after revert: p50 ~8ms (unchanged), p99 dropped from 24ms -> 13ms on the three canaries. chunk-size histogram shows median chunk 512B -> 2KB after revert
ben: that's a pretty clear signal pointing to chunking/coalescing interaction with selector
elaine: great find. we'll keep selector change on hold and write a follow-up RFC for coordinated rollout that includes chunker tuning and kernel selector test vectors
dmitri: filing the RFC now and will attach the chunk histograms + profiler samples. thanks all :thumbsup:
